title: C# gizmo plugin causes crash on exit.
body: ### Tested versions I've reproduced this on the official releases of 4.5-stable and 4.4.1-stable mono builds on Windows 10 and MacOS 15.4.1. ### System information Godot v4.5.stable.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7247) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4790K CPU @ 4.00GHz (8 threads) - 31.93 GiB memory ### Issue description I have a custom type, gizmo for my type, and an editor plugin all written in C#. If the editor ever creates an instance of my gizmo, then the editor crashes on exit with the OS crash dialog "Godot Engine has stopped working". The verbose logs during this process show the following: ``` Unloading addon: res://addons/myaddon/plugin.cfg Editor Plugin exiting tree EditorSettings: Save OK! Unloading: Disposing tracked instances... Fatal error. 0xC0000005 at Godot.NativeInterop.NativeFuncs.godotsharp_internal_refcounted_disposed(IntPtr, IntPtr, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_bool) at Godot.GodotObject.Dispose(Boolean) at Godot.GodotObject.Dispose() at Godot.DisposablesTracker.OnGodotShuttingDownImpl() at Godot.DisposablesTracker.OnGodotShuttingDown() ``` The C++ stack trace shows an access violation somewhere in the disposal process of the gizmo plugin itself. ### Steps to reproduce This appears to be a blanket issue with all node3d gizmo plugins written in C#, however it appears to be very rare in small scenes, possibly because it seems related to a race condition. I've created a MRP project that reproduces the crash on Windows and Mac with high probability. 1. Open the MRP or copy the `myaddon` addon into the addons folder of any project. 2. Build the project. 3. Enable the My Addon plugin. 4. Add a `SetupNode` to a new scene, or open the pre-existing `node_3d.tscn`. 5. Close the Godot editor. The crash should happen here. The `SetupNode` creates 100 children, which seems to increase the chances of the crash to a near certainty. If you lower the 100 down to 5-10, recompile, and repeat with a new scene, you can see that the crash is nondeterministic. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Download the MRP: [mono-gizmo-plugin-crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22476362/mono-gizmo-plugin-crash.zip) It basically just contains a blank `Node3D` subclass `MyType`, a blank `Node3DGizmoPlugin` for that type, and an editor plugin that enables the gizmo. The SetupNode is optional to reproduce, but its purpose is to add 100 `MyType` child nodes to the scene, which is what really seems to cause the crash. The crash does not happen if the gizmo is never instantiated, e.g. if `_HasGizmo` is changed to always return false, or if there are no `MyType` objects in the scene. This appears to be a C#-specific issue, the analogous setup in GDScript does not appear to cause a crash, so rewriting your gizmo plugin in GDScript is a temporary workaround for others experiencing this issue.
